heard: A giant black hole hurled a star out of our galaxy. Astronomers tracked this stellar runaway, known as S-5HVS-1, roughly 29,000 light years away from Earth. Sergey Kopasov and a team of researchers used Gaia spacecraft data to trace its direct path. The star travels at an extraordinary velocity of approximately 1,755 kilometers per second. This speed is more than triple what is required to break free from our home galaxy. It was kicked out of the galactic center approximately five million years ago. Our central black hole, Sagittarius A, captured its partner star and violently slung this one away. Now this lonely outcast is fleeing the Milky Way at nearly four million miles per hour.
